current.text: He had the best season of his career last year, with career highs in scoring and assists. His usage rose from 24 to 28 under David Adelman, and he finished 17th per game.
Teammate absences helped his usage last season, since he was the only one who stayed healthy.
Experts expect his 28 usage and 35 minutes to hold. One calls his role the safest in his point guard tier.
He is a projected starter, next to Christian Braun, Cam Johnson, Aaron Gordon and Nikola Jokic.
Experts draft him in round 2, around picks 19 to 20. They call him good value there and safe in the middle of round 2. He sits in a close tier with Mitchell, Maxey, Ball, Thompson and Johnson.
Experts see upside to a top 12 to 14 finish in 9-cat. One says he could finish ahead of Tyrese Maxey.
Experts say his ESPN rank is far too low and call it free real estate.
In an expert auction mock, he went for 37 USD.
Josh targeted him in that auction but would pay no more than 34 USD.
His three-point shooting of 42 to 43% will probably drop.
He is a fine round 2 pick to pair with Jokic.
Moore thinks Denver could trade him by the deadline to shed salary, because the team cannot build a top-15 defense while paying both Jokic and Murray over 30M USD.
Moore doubts Denver will rest him on purpose.
Denver has 43 games through March 28, one below the max, and only 14 back-to-backs, one of the lowest counts in the league.

durable.text: He is a strong three-point shooter, near 40% or better over the last four years. Around 40 to 41% is a reasonable expectation going forward.
His game has turned more toward playmaking, closer to Tony Parker than a discount Steph Curry.
He has a broad guard category profile: volume scoring, assists, threes and a high FT%, with a good FG% for a guard. No category is weak.

tags.name: trades likely
tags.detail: At least two of last year's starters are expected to be gone by the deadline.

note: Experts treat Murray as a solid round 2 pick with a top 12 to 14 ceiling, and he has no weak category, so he fits any build. Yahoo values him at 40 USD (average cost 37 USD) and ESPN at 36 USD (average cost 25.7 USD), while our league paid 27 USD for him last season, so 34 to 38 USD is a fair range and anything below that is a bargain. Early in the season, check whether his 28 usage holds now that DeRozan has arrived and teammates are healthy, and whether his three-point shooting falls back toward 40%.
